name: cloud-watchdog
description: The my-watchdog panel as an Android app: a WebView showing the REAL dashboard, drawn by my-konsole-dash inside nix-on-droid and transcribed to HTML.
_doc: The app owns no layout. It asks the terminal for a screen at the grid this device actually has and injects what comes back. Every previous attempt to re-draw that dashboard outside the panel diverged on frames, alignment and colour, so nothing here reproduces any of it.

watchdog._doc: Baked into libs:watchdog as WATCHDOG_TARGETS_JSON_B64 / _CMD. Host, port, user and the command are DATA, never Kotlin constants — the same rule cloud-ide's terminal-targets.json follows. Loopback because Android shares 127.0.0.1 across app sandboxes. Auth is key-based and the key is generated in-app: add the public line (Setup screen) to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys in the env.

modules._doc: settings.gradle iterates this (FIRE rule 6: never hardcode the list). `dir` is how a module is SHARED by reference rather than copied: the lib lives once in ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs and every app points at that one directory, so a fix lands in all of them at build time.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Mirrors aa_cloud-superapp / ea_cloud-comms pins so all the Android projects share one toolchain story. Node is added for the Acode (Cordova) fork's JS/plugin build.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-IDE, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): A0_keys/providers/android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A0_keys/providers/android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD telling you to use the one shared key — it never generates or substitutes a random/legacy key.
